newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs sharply higher on financial system concerns.
newsitem.headline: JGBs sharply higher on financial system concerns.

text.p: The key March Japanese government bond futures contract was sharply higher by midday on Wednesday due to market rumours about a major Japanese bank.
Traders said rumours, later denied, that the Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) might hold an emergency news briefing, rekindled worries about Japan's financial system and buying of JGBs.
An NCB official told Reuters that the bank had no plan to hold an emergency news conference.
Despite the denial, the market believes there will still be liquidity problems at some banks and that the Bank of Japan has no choice but hold on to its easy credit policy, traders said.
The March stood at 126.64 by midday, up sharply from the previous day's 126.22. Turnover was 25,998 contracts.

The rise in JGBs was triggered by a fall in NCB's share prices to their lowest level for the current financial year on Wednesday, traders said. The false rumour about a possible emergency media conference also encouraged buying, they said.
Traders said, however, that it was difficult to say how long the current JGB rally would last.
"So far, all that has happened is a rise (in the March) to near the high end of a boxed range," a trader for a trust bank's securities affiliate said.

Although it is hard to predict future movements in JGBs at this point, a try for the upperside is possible, especially since JGBs are firm despite a weakness in the yen versus the dollar, the trader said.
The dollar rose to its highest level in four years against the yen in morning trade on Wednesday.
A temporary rise to an all-time high is possible, but JGBs are likely to have difficulty breaking out of recent ranges in the near-term, a city bank trader said.
The all-time high for any benchmark JGB futures contract is 126.83 set on January 27, 1997.
NCB said on Wednesday that it sees no cause for concern about its financial health.
The bank also said that it would take serious note of the stock market's view of its share price.
The benchmark 182nd JGB yield stood at 2.360 percent as of 0254 GMT, down from the previous day's 2.390 percent.
